newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary O/N market surprised by repo cut - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Hungary O/N market surprised by repo cut - dealers.

text.p: The timing of a 25 basis point cut in the central bank's one-week and one-month reverse repo facilities surprised the market, dealers said.
"The fact itself was not surprising but the way it was done was not entirely fair," said Sandor Tolonics of Commerzbank.
The National Bank of Hungary (NBH) cut its one-week reverse repo rate to 20.00 percent and its one-month reverse repo rate to 20.50 percent at 0632 GMT, while the market was still active.
"Overnight rates dropped to 19.625 percent (from Friday's 20.00 percent close) and market participants were queuing up at the central bank when the announcement came," Tolonics said.
Participants were waiting to deposit their excess funds with the NBH's reverse repo facilities.
Another trader said this was the first time the NBH had cut its repo rates during business."This has never happened before," said Krisztina Hortobagyi of Creditanstalt.
The National Bank of Hungary usually cuts its repo rates on Friday around 1400 hours local time, traders said.
But both traders said neither the size nor the general timing of the cut was a surprise to the market.
